A study of the enrollment from the data in the one available catalog lists students for the year 1887-1888 as follows:

Collegiate Department         66
Preparatory Department       133
Total Enrollment             391³¹

Of this number 151, or approximately fifty per cent, listed Savoy as their permanent home; thirty-six other Texas towns, eleven from Indian Territory, makes these figures represent thirty-six other Texas towns, eleven from Indian Territory, a table that was found that many of the students' homes were approximately forty miles from the college, a distance which at that time represented three or more days' travel with horse and buggy.

THE EVOLUTION OF THE CURRICULUM

The curriculum of Savoy Male and Female College at the time of 1885-1888, the period covered by the evidence extended from the verbal beginnings of schooling—spelling in the Webster's "Blue-Back" Speller—to study through all years of the student's time. To reach Roy's "Third Part Arithmetic" was, according to older students, to accomplish a task not likely to be attained before the age of twelve or thirteen. The highest class of the English language curriculum for 1883-1884 was language through all years. For 1883-1884, together with the addition of two teachers belongs to the "college" faculty; and for the remainder of the years the strictly "college" courses were taught by the two principals.
